reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 33. Nay or No: 6. Not Voting: 1. said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.

posts.text: I would like to express my gratitude to all U.S. veterans, living and deceased, for their service to our country. At the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month of 1918, the Armistice with Germany went into effect, ending the fighting of World War I. This Veterans Day, we commemorate the more than 41 million Americans who have served in our nation’s wars since 1775, and the millions more who have served in peacetime.

We have been tracking the reemergence of the New World screwworm for years. Throughout this time, our team has taken steps to prepare for the chance that this menace will reappear here in the Southwest. 

I believe the steps we have taken by prioritizing funding for monitoring at our ports of entry and requiring USDA to plan for domestic sterile fly production, will provide USDA the tools they need. 

Let's stay vigilant and understand from history the financial impact that not taking swift and decisive action would cost us.

The 2026 fiscal year ended Wednesday. The national debt increased by $2,534,271,606,405. That's $2.53 trillion.

Or:
$6.9 billion a day
$290 million an hour
$4.8 million a minute
$80,000 a second

@BillAckman Legalize innovation.

https://t.co/QYKXzFb1VW

At the beginning of the fiscal year, the 10-year was at 4.1 percent. Today, the 10-year is at 5.1 percent: a 100 basis point movement over a single fiscal year. 

A sustained 60 basis point rise adds roughly $2 trillion in interest over a decade. A sustained 100 basis point https://t.co/UGodKomjJn

We have to show the world’s debt markets we’re serious about our fiscal future or we risk letting them decide our future for us. 

This fiscal year alone, we’ll borrow about $2.5 trillion, $6.9 billion a day, nearly $80,000 every second.

My condolences go out to the Kyl family today.  Senator Jon Kyl will be remembered as a true statesman who always did right by Arizona and America. I was honored to have had the opportunity to serve with him.

The rate on the 10-year Treasury note has reached 5% twice since 2007: briefly in October 2023 and today.

Today's number should scare Congress. In 2007, debt-to-GDP was 62% and the deficit was 1.1%. Now, debt-to-GDP is 123% and the deficit is above 6%.

https://t.co/9XpMJ0PVtQ

At a 5% average interest rate, $63 trillion in debt means about $3.15 trillion a year just to pay interest.

By 2036, that could consume roughly 56% of federal revenue outside payroll taxes.

That’s interest fragility. Eventually you’re borrowing just to cover the cost of past https://t.co/msAPZP98yg

Today, we remember the 2,977 Americans who lost their lives on September 11, 2001, changing our lives forever.  

May we never forget the heroes of 9/11 and the brave sacrifices made by so many to protect their fellow citizens. https://t.co/odbBn61vWq

We went from around 20 copper smelters in the U.S. to two, while China came to dominate much of the critical-mineral processing.

Bringing that processing capacity back means using new extraction and refining technology to leapfrog the old methods and build the next generation of https://t.co/LYILe05J1f

Debt models start crashing when federal debt reaches around 154% of the size of the economy. At current interest rates, we’re headed above 160% in the next decade.

The models put us in the danger zone around 2035. A recession, war or one bad shock can push our borrowing costs https://t.co/fz1ltZbWoc

We’re borrowing roughly $7 billion a day. Too many in Washington still do not understand what that means.

If we keep borrowing at this pace, the bond market will run this country. https://t.co/e40Whe2xrw

My prayers are with the families of those who lost their lives and the crews continuing the search and recovery effort.

Please stay clear of the closed areas and follow @GrandCanyonNPS for the latest updates. https://t.co/CNiMLqN1jw
Congratulations on a remarkable career, John. Always enjoyed our conversations over the years. https://t.co/uZ2LpkbbqQ
In June I said on the House floor we'd cross $40 trillion in debt by the end of this summer work period. We cross it this week. We're borrowing about $93,000 every second. https://t.co/7AXh7z3u79
Thank you to the Dexcom team for the tour of their Mesa manufacturing facility last week. Great to see the technology that helps people manage diabetes being built in Arizona. https://t.co/o24TkTnJsh

Our national debt just hit $39.77 trillion.

It grew by nearly $3 trillion in one year. More than $8 billion every day, $337 million every hour and $93,632 every second.

We are in real trouble. https://t.co/ZXoNsASNYg
Honored to receive the @NRFnews 2026 Hero of Main Street Award. I will always fight for the small businesses and retailers that keep our Main Streets strong. https://t.co/ReMzo2hlv3

Congressman Mitchell and I ran against each other in two very hard-fought elections.

Harry was always civil and decent in a profession that is often anything but. He was a good man who left a lasting legacy on our state.

I want to send my condolences to his children Mark and
Congratulations to Father Tegin Joy Alvarez, who was recently sworn in as a U.S. citizen and proudly serves our country in the military. https://t.co/n1fSV5Edmf

The 30-year Treasury yield is above 5%, and the 10-year is at its highest level in more than a year.

If Congress doesn’t get control of its ravenous borrowing, the bond market is going to run this country. https://t.co/t2GDbMhU4R

Foreign money should not flow through tax-exempt organizations without basic transparency.

Today, @WaysandMeansGOP passed my Foreign Funding Transparency Act to track foreign contributions, with added scrutiny for money from China, Iran, North Korea and Russia. https://t.co/TctVDcH2iF

Washington may be a math-free zone. The bond market is not.

We are borrowing $93,000 every second. The next reconciliation bill has to show the markets that someone in Congress still owns a calculator. https://t.co/GdmwCDlhNX
Thank you to the Institute for Legislative Analysis for recognizing my voting record with its Defender of Limited Government Award. https://t.co/T1J9sMA2w8

It saddens me to share the news that my father Bill Schweikert died this morning

He was a good man, a great father, and a wonderful grandfather to our children Olivia and Matthew.

I will always cherish this picture of him with Matthew that was taken last night just hours before https://t.co/GR0xzAFdvY

Medicaid spending is already up 9.7% this year and could finish in double digits while we borrow about $90,000 a second.

At some point, we have to lower the cost of delivering care instead of asking taxpayers to pay more without people getting healthier. https://t.co/M0oJRprwvp

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
